newsitem.title: SWEDEN: IBCA rates Belgium's ASLK-CGER bank A+ long-term.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Belgium's ASLK-CGER bank A+ long-term.

text.p: European credit ratings agency IBCA said on Monday it assigned an A+ long-term and short-term A1 ratings to Belgian bank ASLK-CGER.
It said in a statement received in Stockholm that it also assigned an individual of B and a legal rating of 2 to the bank.

IBCA said in a statement that the bank's performance had improved steadily since its partial privatisation three years ago with the sale of 49.9 percent of the bank to Fortis, the Belgian/Dutch group.
"The performance of ASLK-CGER Bank has steadily improved as income has risen and costs have been reduced," it said.
It said the bank's strength lay in its market share which was 20 percent for customer funding, which easily exceeds its customer lending.
"The bank also has a large share of the Belgian residential mortgage market; such lending accounts for about half of its loan portfolio," it said.
"A further quarter of the bank's loans are to state bodies and the final quarter to corporates, a lending profile which has contributed to sound asset quality."
IBCA said the bank was reasonably capitalised given the low risk of its weightings and its asset base and is expecting continuing good results in 1996.
